safi-cedvel:7-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (السماء) is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb that is explained by the verb mentioned after it.
The clause «(رفع) السماء ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «علّمه البيان» [Note: in verse (4) of this sūra]. The clause «رفعها ...» has no grammatical position, being explicative. The clause «وضع ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause (رفع), which is implied.
8- (أن) is a particle of the verbal noun (maṣdar) and of the accusative; (لا) is a negation. [Note: it is possible that (أن) is explicative (mufassira) and (لا) is prohibitive ... because the setting of the balance calls for the command to act justly, and this is the statement ...]. (في الميزان) is attached to (تطغوا). The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تطغوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted lām, attached to (وضع), i.e. "so that you do not transgress ...".
The clause «تطغوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle (أن) which forms a maṣdar.
9- (الواو) is parenthetical. (بالقسط) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أقيموا. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is prohibitive and jussive ...
The clause «أقيموا ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical. The clause «لا تخسروا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
10- 13- (الواو) is a conjunction in the four places. (الأرض) is a direct object of an omitted verb that is explained by the verb mentioned after it. (للأنام) is attached to (وضعها). (فيها) is attached to a fronted predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ) (فاكهة). (الفاء) is the connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition. (بأي) is attached to (تكذّبان). [Note: this verse is mentioned thirty-one times. Eight of them come after verses that enumerate the wonders of Allah's creation and the marvels of His handiwork; then seven after verses mentioning the Fire and its terrors; then eight verses describing the two gardens; and another eight describing the two gardens below the first two ... The repetition came for emphasis and reminder.]
The clause «(وضع) الأرض ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «وضع الميزان» [Note: in verse (7) of the sūra].
The clause «وضعها ...» has no grammatical position, being explicative. The clause «فيها فاكهة ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from الأرض. The clause «بأي ... تكذبان» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the matter is as has been detailed, then which of the favours ...".

* Morphology:
(الميزان): the first means justice (al-ʿadl), the second means the instrument for measuring weight, and the third means what is weighed ... See verse (152) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(12) العصف: an inert noun (ism jāmid) for the leaf of every plant from which grain comes out; its pattern (wazn) is فعل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn. (الريحان): it is originally a maṣdar, then was applied to a well-known fragrant plant, and it also means provision (rizq). According to al-Farrāʾ it is the leaf of the crop, and its pattern is فعلان with a fatḥa on the first letter.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (al-takrīr): in the saying of the Exalted فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ.
It is repeated many times in this sūra, and this repetition, when repeated, is sweeter than sugar. It is fitting only as an affirmation of the various, enumerated blessings: whenever He, glory be to Him, mentions a blessing He has bestowed, He rebukes the denial of it, just as a man says to another: "Did I not do you good by granting you wealth? Did I not do you good by doing such and such for you?" Repetition is fitting here because of the difference in what is being affirmed, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.

safi-cedvel:14-16.t:
* I'rab:
(من صلصال) is attached to (خلق). (كالفخّار) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (صلصال). (من مارج) is attached to the second (خلق). (من نار) is attached to an adjective of (مارج) [Note: (من) is explanatory or partitive ... and if المارج means fire, then it is a substitute (badal) with repetition of the preposition]. (فبأي ... تكذّبان) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra], in its words and clauses. The clause «خلق الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «خلق الجانّ ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(الفخّار): a name for what has been baked from clay; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (مارج): a name for what is mixed of red, green and yellow; it was also said that it means the pure, and also said that it is the flickering flame; its pattern is فاعل with a kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject, its implied form being "he" (هو). (فبأي ... ) is like the first, in its words and clauses «1». The clause «(هو) ربّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:19-23.t:
* I'rab:
The agent (fāʿil) of (مرج) is a pronoun referring to Allah. (بينهما) is accusative, attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (برزخ). (لا) is a negation ... (فبأي ... ) is like the first in both places «2», in its words and clauses. (منهما) is attached to (يخرج) ...
The clause «مرج ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يلتقيان ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين. The clause «بينهما برزخ ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين or from the agent of يلتقيان. The clause «لا يبغيان ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين [Note: or from the agent of يلتقيان, or from the pronoun in (بينهما) .. and it carries the sense of giving a reason, i.e. "so that they do not transgress"]. The clause «يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(22) المرجان: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for one of the precious stones; its pattern is فعلان with a fatḥa on the first letter, and its singular is مرجانة. It is red veins like the fingers of the hand; it was also said that it is small pearls.

* Rhetoric:
The art of broadening (fann al-ittisāʿ): in the saying of the Exalted يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ.
He said "from both of them" and did not say "from one of them", because when the two met and became like one thing, it was permissible to say that they come out of both of them, as one says "they come out of the sea" although they do not come out of the whole sea but out of a part of it. You also say "I left the town" when you have left only one quarter of its quarters, indeed one house of its houses.

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (له) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (الجواري); it is nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for the sake of agreement with the reading in connected recitation (waṣl). (في البحر) is attached to (الجواري). (كالأعلام) is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in المنشئات. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra], in its words and clauses ...
The clause «له الجواري ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(المنشآت): plural of المنشأة, the feminine of المنشأ, a passive participle of the quadriliteral (أنشأ); its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted وَلَهُ الْجَوارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلامِ.
Here He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, likened the ships, as they cleave the swell of the sea, going and coming, to towering mountains.

safi-cedvel:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. (عليها) is attached to an omitted ṣila of (من). (فان) is the predicate of the subject, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (ذو) is an adjective of وجه, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «كلّ من عليها فان» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يبقي وجه ربّك ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(26) فان: an active participle of the triliteral (فني), its pattern is فاع, with an elision weakening (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, the quiescence of the yāʾ and the tanwīn.
(27) الجلال: an auditory maṣdar (maṣdar samāʿī) of the triliteral verb جلّ; its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (الإكرام): a regular maṣdar (maṣdar qiyāsī) of the quadriliteral verb أكرم; its pattern is إفعال ...

* Rhetoric:
1- The unrestricted figurative usage (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ.
That is, His Essence, mighty and majestic, and what is meant is He Himself, glory be to Him, the Exalted. The annexation is explanatory (bayāniyya). The literal meaning of "face" in the observable world is the bodily member, and using it for the Essence is an unrestricted figurative usage, like the use of "hands" for "selves".
2- The art of variation (fann al-iftinān): in the saying of the Exalted كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْها فانٍ وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلالِ وَالْإِكْرامِ.
This art is that the speaker varies, bringing in his speech two kinds, either opposed, or different, or agreeing. Here He, glory be to Him, combined consolation and boasting: He consoled all creatures, and praised Himself for being alone in remaining after the passing away of all that exists, while describing His Essence, after His being alone in remaining, with majesty and honour.

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun (من). (كلّ) is a noun indicating time that stands in for the adverb "day" (yawm); it is accusative, attached to the settledness (al-istiqrār) which is the predicate of the subject (هو). (في شأن) is attached to the predicate of the subject (هو). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses «1». The clause «يسأله من في السموات» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «هو في شأن» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to (سنفرغ). (أيّها) is an indefinite specific vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable, in the position of the accusative. (فبأي ... ) is like the first «2». The clause «سنفرغ لكم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «أيّها الثقلان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الثقلان): the dual of ثقل (with two fatḥas), its pattern is فعل; a collective noun for mankind or the jinn, either in the sense of "one who weighs down" (muthqil, with kasra on the qāf), i.e. who weighs down the earth, or in the sense of "one who is burdened" (mathqūl, with fatḥa on the ʿayn), i.e. loaded with obligations and wearied by them.

* Benefits:
The letter hāʾ..
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلانِ. Here (إلها) is an alerting particle (ḥarf tanbīh). We will set out the cases of this letter, in order to clarify what is connected with it. It occurs in five ways: 1- It comes as a pronoun for the third person, and is in the position of the genitive or the accusative, as in the saying of the Exalted: قالَ لَهُ صاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحاوِرُهُ. [Translator's note: the source repeats the verse in the text as "تعالى: قالَ لَهُ صاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحاوِرُهُ" twice; the repetition is a slip in the source.]
The hāʾ of له and of صاحبه is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the hāʾ of يحاوره is in the position of the accusative, a direct object.
2- It comes as a particle of the third person: this is the hāʾ in (إيّاه). The verified view is that it is a particle with merely the meaning of the third person, and that the pronoun is «إيّا» alone.
3- The hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt): this is the one attached to clarify a vowel or a letter, as in (ماهية), and (هاهناه) and (وا زيداه), and the saying of the Exalted: ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ. هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ.
4- The one substituted for the hamza of interrogation, as in the verse:
وأتى صواحبها فقلن: هذا الذي ... منح المودة غيرنا وجفانا
(Her companions came and said: "Is this the one who granted affection to others than us and shunned us?") 
The verified view is that this one should not be counted, because it is not original; moreover some claimed that the original is «هذا» and the alif was dropped.
5- The hāʾ of the feminine, as in (رحمه) in pausal form. This is the opinion of the Kufans. The verified view is that it should not be counted, because it is part of a word, not a word.
As for (ها), it occurs in three ways:
1- A verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning (خذ) "take"; its alif may be lengthened, and both are used with the kāf of address and without it. In the lengthened form it is permissible to dispense with the kāf by inflecting its hamza as the kāf is inflected, so one says (هاء) for the masculine, (هاء) for the feminine with a kasra on the hamza, and (هاؤما), (هاؤنّ), (هاؤم); from this is the saying of the Exalted: هاؤُمُ اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ.
2- It is a pronoun for the feminine, used in the position of the genitive and the accusative, as in the saying of the Exalted: فَأَلْهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْواها; in the first it is in the position of the accusative, and in the other two in the position of the genitive.
3- It is for alerting, and enters upon four things:
1- The demonstrative not specific to the far, as in: (هذا). As for (هنا), the hāʾ is original and is not for alerting.
2- The nominative pronoun about which a demonstrative noun gives information, as in the saying of the Exalted: ها أَنْتُمْ أُولاءِ.
3- The adjective of (أي) in the vocative, as in: (يا أيها الرجل). In the dialect of Banū Asad it is permissible to drop its alif and to give its hāʾ a ḍamma by assimilation, and on this is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir (أيّه المؤمنون) (أيّه الثقلان).
4- The name of Allah the Exalted in an oath when the particle is omitted: one says «ها الله», with the hamza pronounced as a cutting or a connecting hamza, both with the alif of (ها) retained and dropped.

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(استطعتم) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (أن) is a particle of the verbal noun (maṣdar) and of the accusative. (من أقطار) is attached to (تنفذوا). (الفاء) is the connecting particle for the apodosis. (لا) is a negation. (إلّا) is for restriction. (بسلطان) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تنفذون [Note: or attached to (تنفذون)]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra]. The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنفذوا ...) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object.
The clause of the vocative «يا معشر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «إن استطعتم ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative. The clause «تنفذوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle (أن) which forms a maṣdar. The clause «انفذوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ. The clause «لا تنفذون ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you pass through, you will not pass through"].

safi-cedvel:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(عليكما) is attached to (يرسل). (من نار) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (شواظ). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is a negation. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «يرسل عليكما شواظ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «لا تنتصران ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يرسل.

* Morphology:
(شواظ): a name for pure flame, or flame with smoke in it; its pattern is فعال with a ḍamma on the first letter.
(نحاس): a name for the well-known metal, or meaning smoke with no flame in it; its pattern is فعال with a ḍamma on the first letter.

safi-cedvel:37-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive and the second is a conjunction. (إذا) is an adverb of future time, in the position of the accusative, attached to the content of the implied apodosis. (كالدهان) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (وردة) [Note: it may be a second predicate]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses. (الفاء) is a conjunction [Note: or resumptive, or the connecting particle for the preceding apodosis, in which case the clause بأي آلاء ... is parenthetical]. (يومئذ) is an adverb, accusative - or indeclinable on the fatḥa - attached to the negated (يسأل). (لا) is a negation. (عن ذنبه) is attached to (يسأل). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] in its words and clauses ...
The clause «انشقّت السماء ...» is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «كانت ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause انشقت ... The apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "you would see a terrible thing". The clause «لا يسأل ... إنس» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the implied apodosis [Note: or has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of إذا, with what is between them parenthetical].
41- 42- (بسيماهم) is attached to a ḥāl from (المجرمون), the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالنواصي) is the deputy agent [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: "to take" (يؤخذ) is transitive, yet it is made transitive here with the bāʾ because it is given the meaning of "to drag". Another said: one says "I took the forelock" and "I took by the forelock". It is related from the Arabs: "I took the rein" and "I took by the rein", with the same meaning.]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses. The clause «يعرف المجرمون ...» has no grammatical position, being a justification of what precedes. The clause «يؤخذ بالنواصي ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يعرف المجرمون.

* Morphology:
(الدهان): a noun meaning red leather, or what is used for anointing; its pattern is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (وردة): the singular of الورد, which is a generic collective noun (ism jamʿ jinsī); its pattern is فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in the saying of the Exalted: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهانِ.
By "rose" (warda) He meant a reddish hue: in spring the rose leans toward yellow; when the cold intensifies it is a red rose; and after that it is a rose leaning toward dusky grey. So the changing colours of the sky when it splits are likened to the rose, and the rose, in the variety of its colours, is likened to oil and the variety of its colours. The thing likened and that to which it is likened are both sensory, that is, of the type of likening the perceptible to the perceptible. [Translator's note: the source says "الغرس" (planting) for what is meant by "warda"; this seems to be a slip in the source, possibly for "الحمرة" (redness); translated as "reddish hue" from the context of the colours that follow.]

safi-cedvel:43-45.t:
* I'rab:
(التي) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of جهنّم. (بها) is attached to (يكذّب). (بينها) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (يطوفون), and likewise the adverb conjoined to it. (آن) is an adjective of حميم, genitive like it, and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «هذه جهنّم ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl), of an implied saying. The clause «يكذّب بها المجرمون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (التي). The clause «يطوفون ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from جهنّم, the operator in it being the demonstrative.

* Morphology:
(آن): an active participle from the triliteral أني, of the pattern of ضرب, meaning that its heat became intense; its pattern is فاع; it has an elision weakening (iʿlāl) due to the meeting of two quiescent letters.

safi-cedvel:46-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لمن) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (جنّتان). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] in the following eight verses. (ذواتا) is an adjective of (جنّتان), nominative [Note: or the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "they two" (هما), and the clause is an adjective of (جنّتان) with what is between them parenthetical (3, 4); or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive]. (فيهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (عينان), and the second (فيهما) is the predicate of the subject (زوجان). (من كلّ) is attached to a ḥāl from (زوجان) ..
The clause «لمن خاف ... جنّتان» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «خاف ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من). The clause «فيهما عينان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان) «3». The clause «تجريان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (عينان). The clause «فيهما من كلّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان) «4».
54- 55- (متكئين) is an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun of the agent of an omitted verb, and the pronoun refers to those who fear in His saying: لمن خاف, i.e. "they enjoy themselves reclining". (على فرش) is attached to (متّكئين). (من إستبرق) is attached to the predicate of the subject (بطائنها). (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (جني) is a subject (mubtadaʾ), nominative, its predicate being (دان), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun.
The clause «(يتنعّمون) متّكئين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «بطائنها من إستبرق ...» is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of فرش. The clause «جني الجنّتين دان» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl [Note: or conjoined to the clause: فيهما من كلّ فاكهة زوجان].
56- 61- (فيهنّ) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (قاصرات). (قبلهم) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يطمثهنّ). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is redundant, to emphasise the negation. (جان) is conjoined to أنس, nominative. (هل) is a particle of interrogation carrying the meaning of negation. (إلّا) is for restriction.
The clause «فيهنّ قاصرات ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The clause «لم يطمثهنّ إنس ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from قاصرات الطرف, the operator in it being the settledness (al-istiqrār). The clause «كأنّهنّ الياقوت ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from قاصرات الطرف. The clause «هل جزاء ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(48) ذواتا: dual of ذوات - which is originally a singular without dropping the wāw - and the lām of ذوات is a yāʾ, its ʿayn a wāw, and its fāʾ a dhāl, because the original is ذوي - with a yāʾ at the end - in which there is an iʿlāl, because the yāʾ was vowelled and what precedes it had a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif, giving ذوا; then a tāʾ was added at its end. (أفنان): plural of فنن, a name for the branch; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and the pattern of أفنان is أفعال. (54) جنى: a name for fruit, or for what is gathered of honey or gold; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and it has an iʿlāl by substitution, its original being جني: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and turned into an alif.
(58) الياقوت: a name for the precious red-coloured gem; its pattern is فاعول.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted, summarised simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mujmal): in the saying of the Exalted كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْياقُوتُ وَالْمَرْجانُ.
He likened them to the ruby (yāqūt) in the redness of the face, and to the coral (marjān), that is small pearls, in the whiteness of the skin and its clarity; the specifying of the small ones is because they are more intensely white than the large.
Al-Bayhaqī related in al-Baʿth on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The woman among the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) will have the marrow of her shin seen from behind the flesh and bone, from beneath seventy garments, as red wine is seen in a white glass."

safi-cedvel:62-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (من دونهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (جنّتان). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra] in the following eight places. (مدهامّتان) is an adjective of (جنّتان), nominative, and what is between the adjective and the qualified noun is parenthetical ...
The clause «من دونهما جنّتان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
66- 70- (فيهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (عينان), and the second (فيهما) is the predicate of (فاكهة), and (فيهنّ) is the predicate of خيرات ...
The clause «فيهما عينان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical. The clause «فيهما فاكهة ...» is in the position of the nominative, a third adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical. The clause «فيهنّ خيرات ...» is in the position of the nominative, a fourth adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical.
72- 78- (حور) is a substitute (badal) for خيرات, nominative. (مقصورات) is an adjective of حور, nominative. (في الخيام) is attached to (مقصورات). (لم يطمثهنّ ... ولا جانّ): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (56) of the sūra]. (متّكئين على رفرف) is like متكئين على فرش [Note: in verse (54) of the sūra]. (ذي) is an adjective of ربّك, genitive ...
The clause «لم يطمثهنّ إنس ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of حور. The clause «(يتنعّمون) متّكئين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: the pronoun in the verb refers to the spouses (al-azwāj) understood from the context of the verses]. The clause «تبارك اسم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(64) مدهامّتان: dual of مدهامة, the feminine of مدهامّ ... It is an active participle of the sextiliteral verb ادهامّ - or a passive participle of it - and both meanings suit the noble verse; its pattern is افعالّ.
(66) نضّاختان: dual of نضّاخة, the feminine of نضّاخ, an intensive form of the active participle, from the triliteral نضخ; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (70) خيرات: plural of خيرة, of the pattern فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, or plural of خيرة with a fatḥa and a kasra, which is a lightened form of خيّرة with shadda; both words are an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral خار يخير, and they are two adjectives of an omitted qualified noun, by which are meant the women of Paradise, the wide-eyed maidens (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn). (حسان): a broken plural of حسناء, an assimilated adjective from the triliteral حسن of the pattern of كرم; its pattern is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (72) مقصورات: plural of مقصورة, the feminine of مقصور, a passive participle from the triliteral قصر, meaning "to screen"; its pattern is مفعول. One says "a woman is qaṣīra, qaṣūra and maqṣūra", i.e. veiled in seclusion. (الخيام): plural of خيم, which is a plural of خيمة, that is, it is a plural of a plural; the pattern of خيمة is فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, the pattern of خيم is فعل with a kasra and then a fatḥa, and the pattern of خيام is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (76) رفرف: a collective noun (ism jamʿ), whose singular is رفرفة, or a collective generic noun (ism jins jamʿī); it is what hangs down from the couches of precious cloths; its pattern is فعلل, and the collective noun is فعلل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn in each of them. (عبقري): a collective noun whose singular is عبقريّة, or a collective generic noun; the ʿabqarī is the perfect of everything ... Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: it is the eminent and precious among men. It was also said: ʿabqarī is related to ʿAbqar, which the Arabs claim is the name of a land of the jinn, so they relate to it everything wondrous ... Quṭrub said: it is not a relative adjective but is in the position of al-kursī, so the doubled yāʾ is not the yāʾ of relation (nisba).

* Rhetoric:
Specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ): in the saying of the Exalted: فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ.
He conjoined the date-palm and the pomegranate to "fruit", although they are part of it, as a specification of them and a clarification of their excellence, as if, because of their distinction, they were two other kinds. From this is the saying of Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him: if a man swears not to eat fruit and then eats a pomegranate or fresh dates, he does not break his oath, and his two companions differed from him.

* Benefits:
- Writing the hamza..
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ. In the word (متكئين) the hamza is written on a "seat" (nabra, the tooth of the yāʾ). We shall clarify below the most important matters connected with that rule:
1- The hamza at the beginning of a word is written on an alif; it is above the alif if it has a fatḥa or a ḍamma, such as (أمن) (أصول), and below the alif if it has a kasra, such as (إسلام).
2- The hamza in the middle of a word: we compare its vowel with the vowel of the letter before it and write it on the letter that suits the stronger of the two vowels. The strongest of the vowels is the kasra, followed by the ḍamma, followed by the fatḥa. The kasra is suited by the nabra, the ḍamma by the wāw, and the fatḥa by the alif.
In the word (متكئين) the hamza has a kasra and what precedes it has a kasra, so it is written on a nabra. In the word (ينأون) the hamza has a fatḥa and what precedes it is quiescent, and the fatḥa is stronger and is suited by the alif. And so on ...
- Exceptions to the rule for writing the medial hamza.
1- The hamza with a fatḥa preceded by a quiescent alif is written on the line: عباءة - إضاءة - إساءة.
2- The hamza with a fatḥa or a ḍamma preceded by a quiescent wāw is written on the line, such as سموءل - موءودة.
3- The hamza with a fatḥa, a ḍamma or a kasra preceded by a quiescent yāʾ is written on a nabra, such as: ييئس - سرّني مجّيئك - سررت بمجيئك.
3- [Translator's note: the source numbers this item "3" a second time; it is evidently item 4 of the list] The hamza at the end of a word: if it is preceded by a vowelled letter it is written on a letter that suits the vowel of what precedes it, such as: (ناشئ) تباطؤ - ملجأ. If it is preceded by a quiescent letter it is written on the line if it has a ḍamma or a kasra, such as: عبء or عبء, بطء or بطء. If it has a tanwīn of fatḥa, it is written on a nabra if it can be connected to the letter before it, such as:
عبئا - بطئا. If it cannot be connected, it is written on the line, with the tanwīn drawn after it on the alif, such as: جزءا - ردءا, except when it is preceded by a quiescent alif, in which case the tanwīn is drawn above the hamza, such as: رداء - جزاء.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(القرآن) is a second direct object, and the first object is omitted, its implied form being "whomever He willed" [Note: or Jibrīl, or Muḥammad, peace be upon him, or the human being, as indicated by «خلق الإنسان»] ...
Clause: «الرحمن علّم القرآن ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause. And the clause: «علّم ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الرحمن). And the clause: «خلق ... » is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar. And the clause: «علّمه البيان ... » is in the position of the nominative, a third khabar.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بحسبان) is attached to an omitted element, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they run by a reckoning" [Note: which is a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ), or attached to a general being (kawn ʿāmm), with an omitted muḍāf in the mubtadaʾ: "the running of the sun and the moon.."]. Clause: «الشمس ... بحسبان» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical [Note: because the implied clause (رفع) السماء is conjoined to the clause علّمه البيان]. And the clause: «النجم ... يسجدان» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the parenthetical clause. And the clause: «يسجدان» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (النجم ...).

* Morphology:
(النجم) is the name of the plant that has no stem; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa and then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ.
What is meant by their prostration is their submission to Him, Exalted is He, in what He wills of them by their natural disposition; their running according to what their nature requires is likened to the submission of one prostrating to his Creator and his glorifying Him. Then the name of the thing likened to was used for the thing likened. So there is here an explicit derivative metaphor.
2- The art of tawhīm (suggestion of a misleading sense): in His words, Exalted is He, وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ.
This art is the speaker's bringing a word that makes the rest of the speech, before it or after it, suggest that the speaker intended a shared word with another, or intended its mis-writing or alteration, or a difference in its i'rab, or in its meaning, or some other kind of difference, whereas the matter is the opposite. Mention of the sun and the moon suggests to the hearer that النجم is one of the stars of the sky, whereas what is meant is the plant that has no stem.
